summary: Exim container startup fails if the log/spool paths are not owned by the Exim runtime user or if config mutations are appended in the wrong section of /usr/exim/configure.
symptom: The daemon restarts with log permission errors or an 'auth name missing' configuration parse error.
root_cause: Exim expects writable log/spool paths for its runtime user, and blindly appending main-config options to the end of configure can land inside later configuration sections such as authenticators.
successful_path: Before daemon start, chown /var/log/exim and /var/spool/exim to the exim user, and avoid appending keep_environment at the end of configure unless it is inserted in the main section intentionally.
fix: Chown /var/log/exim and /var/spool/exim to exim in the container entrypoint before starting the daemon.
Do not append keep_environment at the end of /usr/exim/configure.
precheck: Verify runtime log and spool directories are writable by the exim user before starting -bd.
If modifying /usr/exim/configure, inspect the section boundaries first.
anti_pattern: Do not assume root-owned touched log files are acceptable to Exim's runtime behavior in containers.
Do not append main options to the very end of configure without checking whether the parser is inside an authenticator or router block.
quick_checks: If Exim exits with 'Cannot open main log file', fix ownership on /var/log/exim and /var/spool/exim first.
If Exim reports 'auth name missing' after a config mutation, inspect the last lines of /usr/exim/configure for misplaced directives.

summary: When the Kong compose template references the same kong image for runtime and both migration services, the first compose up can waste time in noisy duplicate pulls; pre-pulling the shared image once and re-running compose shortens the official path without changing topology.
symptom: The initial compose up spends a long time repeatedly pulling the same kong image for multiple services before any local image is materialized.
root_cause: The compose stack defines kong, kong-migrations, and kong-migrations-up against the same image, so an uncached first run can spend time on redundant shared-image pull work.
successful_path: If the first uncached compose up is dominated by repeated shared-image pulls and no local image appears yet, stop it, docker pull the shared kong image and postgres base image once, then re-run the same official compose command.
fix: Pre-pull postgres:9.5 and kong:latest once, then rerun docker compose up.
Keep the compose topology unchanged after the images are cached.
precheck: Before retrying a slow first compose up, check whether docker images still shows no kong image locally.
Differentiate between slow progress and a genuinely redundant multi-service shared-image pull pattern.
anti_pattern: Do not patch the official compose services just to avoid the shared-image pull behavior when a one-time pre-pull is enough.
Do not misclassify noisy repeated pull status lines as an application startup failure.
quick_checks: If the compose stack uses the same image for app and migration services, pre-pull it once before the retry.
Verify docker images shows the shared image locally before rerunning compose.

summary: Joomla's locked Composer dependencies require PHP ext-ldap; composer install fails until the app runtime enables ldap support.
symptom: composer install aborts with a platform error stating symfony/ldap requires ext-ldap.
root_cause: The Joomla lockfile includes symfony/ldap, so the runtime must expose PHP's ldap extension even if the initial minimal PHP module set looks sufficient for the installer.
successful_path: Install libldap2-dev in the app image, configure docker-php-ext-configure ldap --with-libdir=lib/x86_64-linux-gnu, enable the ldap extension, rebuild the image, and rerun composer install.
fix: Add libldap2-dev and the PHP ldap extension before rerunning composer install.
Rebuild the runtime image instead of bypassing Composer with --ignore-platform-req=ext-ldap.
precheck: Run composer install once early enough to surface locked extension requirements before proceeding to runtime installation.
Check php -m for ldap in Joomla source deployments that use the repo lockfile.
anti_pattern: Do not ignore the ext-ldap platform requirement to force Composer through; fix the runtime image instead.
quick_checks: If composer mentions symfony/ldap or ext-ldap, verify ldap appears in php -m before retrying.
A successful composer install should proceed to Joomla's post-install FIDO cache update.

summary: Drupal main rejects SQLite 3.40.1 from Debian bookworm; use a base image with SQLite >= 3.45 such as php:8.5-cli-trixie before retrying the official CLI install.
symptom: Drupal install stops with a requirements error saying the database server version 3.40.1 is less than the minimum required version 3.45.
root_cause: The current drupal/drupal main branch requires SQLite >= 3.45, but php:8.5-cli-bookworm ships libsqlite3 3.40.1.
fix: Switch the PHP runtime base to a newer distro carrying SQLite >= 3.45.
Rebuild on php:8.5-cli-trixie, which ships SQLite 3.46.1.
precheck: Check Drupal's current SQLite minimum in core/INSTALL.txt or installer output.
Inspect the candidate image's libsqlite3 package version before relying on the quick-start SQLite path.
anti_pattern: Retrying the same bookworm-based image after the installer has already reported the SQLite minimum-version failure.
quick_checks: Run the installer once and read the exact minimum-version message before choosing a different database path.
Prefer a distro-level fix when the official repo flow already assumes SQLite.

summary: Roundcube login verification can fail misleadingly when GreenMail is left on test-offset ports or its seeded user syntax is wrong; use GreenMail standard ports and full-email login mode.
symptom: Roundcube shows a working login page, but authenticated login fails with storage-server warnings or confusing mailbox credential behavior.
root_cause: GreenMail test mode exposes IMAP/SMTP on nonstandard ports, and the seeded user string must be supplied in GreenMail's documented local-part:password@domain format when email-address login is required.
successful_path: Run GreenMail in standard-port mode, set -Dgreenmail.users=demo:DemoPass123!@example.test with -Dgreenmail.users.login=email, keep Roundcube imap_host=mail and smtp_server=mail with smtp_port=25, then verify inbox login with the documented full email credentials.
fix: Switch GreenMail from test-offset ports to standard ports for Roundcube verification.
Use the documented GreenMail user syntax and enable users.login=email when Roundcube logs in with a full email address.
precheck: Check mail-server startup logs to confirm the actual IMAP/SMTP ports and seeded-user interpretation before debugging Roundcube itself.
If the login page works but mailbox auth fails, verify the test mailbox credentials directly against the mail service assumptions.
anti_pattern: Assuming GreenMail's test-offset ports will be consumed automatically by Roundcube without explicit matching runtime configuration.
Passing a full email address before the colon in GreenMail's user definition and assuming that string is the password-bearing login declaration.
quick_checks: Inspect GreenMail logs for the resolved startup ports and any auto-created user messages.
Confirm Roundcube can reach an authenticated Inbox view, not just an anonymous login form.

summary: When setting WordPress `FS_METHOD`, write the quoted string `'direct'`; a bare `direct` constant breaks bootstrap and blocks `wp-cli` from loading WordPress.
symptom: `wp-cli` fails with `Undefined constant "direct"` after writing `FS_METHOD` in `wp-config.php`.
root_cause: Writing `FS_METHOD` as a raw bare token produces invalid PHP for WordPress bootstrap; the value must be a quoted string constant.
successful_path: Set `FS_METHOD` to `'direct'` in `wp-config.php`, then rerun `wp core install` and subsequent verification commands.
fix: Write `define( 'FS_METHOD', 'direct' );` in `wp-config.php` instead of an unquoted bare token.
If bootstrap is already broken, repair the config first before rerunning `wp-cli` commands.
precheck: After generating `wp-config.php`, inspect custom constants before assuming WordPress itself is broken.
anti_pattern: Using a raw unquoted token for string-valued WordPress constants in `wp-config.php`.
quick_checks: If `wp-cli` reports `Undefined constant`, inspect the most recently written custom constants in `wp-config.php`.
Keep `FS_METHOD` as `'direct'` when the goal is local file writes without FTP.

summary: The upstream Alerta API image does not include wget, so a Compose healthcheck that shells out to wget will keep the container unhealthy even when the API is actually serving requests.
symptom: The API container serves /config successfully but Compose still reports unhealthy.
root_cause: The copied healthcheck invoked wget, which is absent from ghcr.io/alerta/alerta-api:latest.
successful_path: Use a Python-based healthcheck inside the container, for example urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8080/config').status == 200.
fix: Replace wget-based checks with python-based HTTP checks in the compose healthcheck.
precheck: If Compose shows unhealthy, confirm whether the image actually contains the healthcheck binary before changing app code.
anti_pattern: Do not assume wget or curl exists in upstream runtime images.
Do not treat an unhealthy flag as app failure without checking the endpoint directly.
quick_checks: docker inspect ...State.Health should go healthy after replacing the wget probe.
GET /config from the host with --noproxy '*' should still return 200.

summary: Once FileRun reaches the installer, a missing license key is an external prerequisite, not an auto-fixable deployment failure.
symptom: The container stack is healthy and the installer page loads, but installation cannot proceed past the license step.
root_cause: FileRun requires a valid product license key during installation, and the server explicitly rejects empty license submissions.
successful_path: After verifying the stack and installer assets are healthy, classify the run as conditional success and document the license requirement if POST /index.php/app/Core/install/!admin/!actions/license_check returns the missing-license response.
fix: POST to the license_check endpoint to confirm the precise blocker before retrying anything else.
Use COMPLETED_CONDITIONAL_SUCCESS when the response is the missing-license message and the rest of the runtime is healthy.
Skip Phase 5.5 and Phase 6 when the app is still installer-blocked by the external license prerequisite.
precheck: Read the official FileRun docker README first; it states that using the software requires a license.
Before attempting remediation, verify whether the installer failure is actually the license gate.
anti_pattern: Do not burn retry budget trying random container or database changes after the license_check endpoint reports the missing-key message.
Do not treat the installation page alone as a fully usable deployment that is ready for the primary audit gate or portable extraction.
quick_checks: POST /index.php/app/Core/install/!admin/!actions/license_check without a key and inspect the JSON body.
Confirm GET / still returns the installation page and installer assets still return 200 before classifying the outcome.
Record the required manual next step and DB settings in README_DEPLOY.md.

summary: File Browser user-management commands can time out when they target the live BoltDB file while the server is running; mutate the database offline instead.
symptom: Running `filebrowser users update` or similar commands against `/database/filebrowser.db` from a second process while the app container is live returns `Error: timeout`.
root_cause: The live server process holds the BoltDB file lock, so concurrent writes from another CLI process cannot acquire the database lock in time.
successful_path: Stop the File Browser app briefly, then run one-shot CLI containers against the mounted /database/filebrowser.db to update the admin password or add users, restart the app, and verify over HTTP.
fix: Do database mutations with the server stopped.
With docker compose run app, pass the subcommand directly because the service entrypoint is already the filebrowser binary.
precheck: If a live CLI write returns `Error: timeout`, treat it as a BoltDB lock symptom before changing the application.
Check the image entrypoint before repeating the binary name in `docker compose run`.
anti_pattern: Do not keep retrying live user mutations against the mounted BoltDB file while the app is running.
Do not run `docker compose run app filebrowser ...`; the service already enters the filebrowser binary.
quick_checks: After offline mutation and restart, admin POST /api/login should succeed with the deterministic password.
GET /api/users with the admin token should reflect the updated account set.

summary: For MinIO repository targets, the older quay.io/minio/minio reference from repository compose examples may be stale; verify the current official image registry path directly before changing the deployment architecture.
symptom: The initial compose pull fails with quay.io/minio/minio not found even though the official MinIO image is still available elsewhere.
root_cause: Repository examples can lag the currently published registry location, causing a false deployment failure before runtime even starts.
successful_path: When the older quay.io MinIO reference fails with not found, verify the live official image path with docker manifest inspect or docker pull against Docker Hub minio/minio, then pin the resolved digest and continue the same image-first deployment flow.
fix: Verify the current official registry path before redesigning the deployment.
Pin the resolved Docker Hub digest once the image pull succeeds.
precheck: If a repository example references quay.io/minio/minio, confirm that tag still exists before treating the deployment as broken.
Use direct image-manifest or pull evidence to separate registry drift from application startup issues.
anti_pattern: Do not pivot into source builds or unrelated remediation when the only failure evidence is a stale image registry reference.
quick_checks: A successful docker pull minio/minio:latest is enough to prove the official image path is still healthy on this host.
After the pull succeeds, pin the digest and rerun the original container deployment path unchanged.

summary: A restored Bytebase portable bundle can fail on first boot if extracted embedded Postgres files under pgdata keep the wrong ownership; normalize ownership before startup and delete the extracted tree through Docker-aware cleanup.
symptom: Portable redeploy verification fails during startup after extracting the initialized runtime archive.
root_cause: The extracted pgdata directory can retain host-side ownership that blocks the embedded Postgres process inside the Bytebase container.
fix: Patch bundle startup to normalize extracted runtime ownership before starting Bytebase.
Remove the temporary extracted source tree through Docker-aware cleanup after successful verification.
precheck: Before first portable redeploy, inspect the bundle's extracted pgdata ownership assumptions.
Require one clean redeploy from bundle artifacts only, not from leftover extracted state.
anti_pattern: Do not assume a tar-restored pgdata tree will boot correctly without ownership correction.
Do not leave the expanded source/runtime tree in the final portable directory.
quick_checks: After bundle deploy, GET /v1/actuator/info should return the expected version and workspace.
After verify, ensure Deliverable/bytebase-final/source is absent.

summary: The official GoCD server and agent images can fail immediately on bind-mounted runtime paths when /godata is not writable by the image user; named volumes avoid the trap.
symptom: Container startup fails with mkdir permission errors under /godata and /home/go.
root_cause: Host bind mounts inherit host ownership and can be unwritable to the GoCD container entrypoint user.
fix: Replace host bind mounts with Docker-managed named volumes for /godata and /home/go.
precheck: If using bind mounts, verify they are writable by the official image user before startup.
Prefer named volumes for first-pass official image validation.
anti_pattern: Assuming empty local directories are safe bind mounts for GoCD runtime paths.
quick_checks: If logs show 'cannot mkdir ... /godata ... Permission denied', switch to named volumes before deeper debugging.

signature: official GitHub release downloads that fail mid-transfer with HTTP/2 PROTOCOL_ERROR can often be recovered by resuming with curl --http1.1 -C -
summary: When GitHub release asset downloads fail mid-stream with HTTP/2 PROTOCOL_ERROR, resume the same official artifact with HTTP/1.1 and byte-range continuation instead of restarting or changing sources.
symptom: The official release tarball download progresses for several minutes and then aborts with curl error 92 and HTTP/2 PROTOCOL_ERROR.
root_cause: Long GitHub release-asset transfers can drop the HTTP/2 stream, especially on slower links.
successful_path: Keep the same official GitHub release URL, resume with curl --http1.1 -L -C -, and verify the completed file against the published SHA-256 checksum before using it in the build.
fix: Retry the same official artifact with curl --http1.1 and -C - to resume the partial file.
Verify the finished artifact against jx-checksums.txt before rebuilding.
precheck: Capture the exact curl failure signature and keep the partial file rather than deleting it immediately.
Fetch the project's published checksum line before trusting a resumed artifact.
anti_pattern: Discarding a large partially downloaded official artifact and restarting from byte zero after every transient GitHub transfer failure.
Switching to an unofficial mirror just to work around a transport error.
quick_checks: If curl exits with code 92, inspect whether the partial file exists and is growing.
After resume completes, compare sha256sum output with the upstream checksum file.

summary: When Docker image download/unpack throughput is extremely low on this host, both custom Redmine runtime images and the official Redmine Alpine image can fail to reach container startup within practical deployment time.
symptom: Build/pull commands stay in image layer download or unpack for extended periods and never reach Redmine initialization.
root_cause: Host-side Docker registry throughput and image unpack speed are too low to complete required image acquisition in time, independent of Redmine application logic.
fix: Prefer checking official image availability and pull rate before investing in source-first container builds.
If both custom and official image paths stall in image acquisition, stop early and classify the task as environment-blocked rather than continuing application-level remediation.
precheck: Probe one official base/app image pull before designing a multi-image deploy path when host throughput is uncertain.
Treat prolonged layer download plus unpack delay as an environment gate, not as a Redmine install issue.
anti_pattern: Spending retries on Redmine configuration changes while Docker has not yet produced a runnable image locally.
quick_checks: Verify that at least one large image layer completes at a usable rate before committing to container-based remediation.
If official and custom image paths both stall before container startup, fail as image-pull infrastructure blockage.

summary: For the Travis CI organization target, the public GitHub URL does not expose a runnable product repo; the official self-hosted path is Travis CI Enterprise 3.x and it is blocked without a vendor-issued license and separate Core Services plus Worker infrastructure.
symptom: A GitHub organization URL appears deployable at first glance, but the referenced public repo is only an issue tracker and the vendor docs route operators to a proprietary enterprise install.
root_cause: The user target identifies the Travis CI organization rather than a public runnable product, and the official self-hosted offering requires proprietary licensing and multi-host infrastructure.
successful_path: Resolve the target through the upstream README and official docs first; if the official product is enterprise-only and license-gated, stop before ad hoc deployment and document the exact prerequisites.
fix: Read the public README before cloning subcomponent repos; confirm whether the target repo is actually the product entrypoint.
Check the official vendor docs for a supported self-hosted path and required licensing before designing any runtime.
If the official path is license-gated, record the blocker and required inputs instead of assembling an unsupported local stack.
precheck: For organization URLs, verify whether the canonical README identifies a deployable product or only an issue tracker/community entrypoint.
Search the vendor docs for licensing and topology requirements before provisioning containers or VMs.
anti_pattern: Do not stitch together public Travis subcomponent repositories into a fake single-node deployment when the official self-hosted product is a separate licensed enterprise distribution.
quick_checks: If the upstream README says 'central issue tracker', stop treating that repo as the deployment source.
If the official docs require a license or trial license plus separate worker infrastructure, treat missing vendor access as a hard blocker.

summary: Gogs rejects the username `admin` during CLI bootstrap because it is reserved, so deterministic admin seeding should use a different name such as `gogsadmin`.
symptom: `gogs admin create-user --name admin` fails immediately during first-run user bootstrap.
root_cause: Gogs treats `admin` as a reserved username and refuses to create the account.
fix: Use a non-reserved deterministic admin account name such as `gogsadmin`.
precheck: Avoid `admin` as the seeded username before running `gogs admin create-user`.
anti_pattern: Retrying the same bootstrap command with `--name admin` after the first reserved-name failure.
quick_checks: If user creation fails, inspect the CLI error before changing config.
Seed the admin account with `gogsadmin` or another non-reserved name.

summary: On the current Buildbot Debian worker image, python3-twisted provides trial3 rather than trial, and mounting an empty host directory on /buildbot hides the image's bundled buildbot.tac and breaks worker startup.
symptom: The worker either fails with 'trial: not found' during the sample shell step or crashes on startup with buildbot.tac missing after an empty /buildbot bind mount is applied.
root_cause: Debian packages install /usr/bin/trial3 instead of trial, and the worker image expects its own preloaded /buildbot contents including buildbot.tac.
fix: Extend the worker image to install python3-twisted and add a /usr/local/bin/trial wrapper or symlink that resolves to /usr/bin/trial3.
Do not mount an empty host directory onto /buildbot for the primary worker deployment unless you also seed buildbot.tac and the expected worker basedir contents.
precheck: Inside the worker container, check command -v trial before verifying the sample build.
Inspect the worker image startup path and avoid masking /buildbot with an empty bind mount.
anti_pattern: Treating python3-twisted installation as sufficient without confirming whether the worker command path is trial or trial3.
Binding an empty host runtime directory over /buildbot and expecting the worker image to regenerate buildbot.tac automatically.
quick_checks: docker exec buildbot-worker-1 sh -lc 'command -v trial' should return a path.
docker logs buildbot-worker-1 should show 'Connected to buildmaster; worker is ready'.

summary: kapp live verification can fail or become misleading if kapp deploy omits -n, if the app namespace does not exist before deploy, or if the app name collides with a managed ConfigMap name such as simple-app in the repo example.
symptom: kapp inspect reports the app in another namespace, deploy fails because the target namespace does not exist, or the step-2 update errors with a disallowed kapp.k14s.io/is-app label on ConfigMap/simple-app.
root_cause: kapp stores app state in the namespace passed to -n, that namespace must exist before the deploy starts, and using an app name identical to a managed ConfigMap collides with kapp's own app-state naming.
successful_path: Pre-create the target namespace with kubectl, always pass -n <namespace> consistently to kapp commands, and use a distinct app name such as apdv-kapp instead of simple-app for the example update flow.
fix: Create the app namespace before the first kapp deploy -n ... .
Keep kapp app state and workload resources in the same intended namespace by passing -n on deploy, inspect, and delete.
Choose an app name that does not collide with example resource names.
precheck: If manifests include a ConfigMap named like the sample app, avoid reusing that name for the kapp app record.
Before the first deploy, make sure the target namespace already exists if you plan to pass -n.
anti_pattern: Do not assume a manifest-created Namespace is enough for kapp app-state creation in the same command.
Do not reuse simple-app as the kapp app name for the repo's second-step example.
quick_checks: kubectl get ns <ns> should succeed before kapp deploy -n <ns>.
kapp inspect -a <app> -n <ns> --tree should not hint that the app exists in another namespace.
The step-2 deploy should create ConfigMap/simple-app successfully without a disallowed-label error.

summary: For modern Actions Runner Controller, a healthy controller-only install is not enough; the official runner scale set chart hard-requires githubConfigSecret, so missing GitHub auth should be treated as an external blocker and classified as conditional success instead of triggering more cluster remediation.
symptom: The controller chart deploys and the ARC CRDs are installed, but the official runner scale set step cannot render or install because no PAT or GitHub App credentials were provided.
root_cause: The upstream gha-runner-scale-set chart requires githubConfigUrl plus a non-empty githubConfigSecret for GitHub API authentication; this prerequisite is external to the cluster deployment.
successful_path: Install and verify the controller first, attempt the runner scale set step with the intended values shape, and if githubConfigSecret is unavailable, stop with documented next steps and COMPLETED_CONDITIONAL_SUCCESS instead of retrying unrelated cluster or chart changes.
fix: Document the missing GitHub PAT or GitHub App credentials as the blocking requirement.
Capture the exact Helm error from gha-runner-scale-set/templates/githubsecret.yaml as evidence.
Do not proceed to bundle extraction when the primary audit fails for the missing credential gate.
precheck: Check task extras and environment for GitHub PAT or App credentials before planning a full ARC initialization.
Confirm the controller chart and runner scale set chart are both part of the current official flow.
anti_pattern: Do not keep retrying kind, Helm, or controller settings after the runner scale set chart fails specifically on missing githubConfigSecret.
Do not classify a controller-only install as a full official ARC success when no AutoscalingRunnerSet exists.
quick_checks: kubectl get deployment -n arc-system arc-gha-rs-controller should show the controller available.
helm upgrade --install for gha-runner-scale-set with an empty secret should fail at githubsecret.yaml, proving the missing external prerequisite.
kubectl get autoscalingrunnersets,autoscalinglisteners,ephemeralrunnersets,ephemeralrunners -A should be empty when the credential gate has not been satisfied.

summary: Kraken's official devcluster assumes Docker-for-Mac host.docker.internal behavior; on Linux, herd self-calls should resolve host.docker.internal to 127.0.0.1 while agent containers should resolve it to the Docker bridge gateway.
symptom: Proxy/build-index/agent calls to host.docker.internal return EOF or empty replies even though published ports are up.
root_cause: Docker's synthetic host.docker.internal mapping on this Linux host does not satisfy both herd self-calls and agent-to-host bridge calls at the same time.
fix: Add --add-host host.docker.internal:127.0.0.1 to the herd container startup.
Add --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway to the agent container startups.
precheck: From the herd container, curl http://host.docker.internal:15002/ and require an HTTP response instead of Empty reply from server.
From an agent container, curl http://172.17.0.1:15004/ and require an HTTP response.
anti_pattern: Do not reuse the same host.docker.internal mapping for both herd self-calls and agent bridge calls on Linux.
quick_checks: docker exec kraken-herd curl -sv http://host.docker.internal:15002/ should reach nginx.
docker exec kraken-agent-one curl -sv http://host.docker.internal:15004/ should reach build-index through the bridge gateway.

summary: Modern Docker 29 pushes OCI image manifests by default; Kraken's build-index must accept OCI manifest and OCI index media types or proxy pushes fail during tag publication.
symptom: docker push to the Kraken proxy uploads blobs but fails during manifest/tag publication with mediaType mismatches.
root_cause: The upstream dockerutil parser only accepted Docker distribution schema2 manifest/list media types and rejected equivalent OCI media types.
fix: Normalize OCI manifest and OCI index media types onto the existing schema2/manifest-list parsing path.
Advertise both Docker and OCI manifest media types in the Accept header set.
precheck: If docker push reports blob uploads succeeded but manifest publication fails, inspect build-index logs for OCI mediaType errors.
Run a targeted go test for ./utils/dockerutil after patching manifest parsing.
anti_pattern: Do not assume Docker pushes schema2 media types on current Docker releases.
quick_checks: docker push localhost:15000/<repo>:<tag> should print a final digest instead of unknown error.
go test ./utils/dockerutil should pass with OCI fixture coverage.

summary: A bind-mounted Laminar home directory can make the dashboard and job discovery look healthy while `laminarc run` fails with `Peer disconnected` if the in-container `laminar` user cannot write the SQLite DB, run directories, and archive directories.
symptom: Dashboard `GET /` and `laminarc show-jobs` succeed, but `laminarc run <job>` fails with `Peer disconnected` and no run/archive state appears.
root_cause: The mounted `/var/lib/laminar` tree is readable but not writable by UID/GID `999`, so Laminar cannot create `laminar.sqlite`, run directories, or archived artifacts during actual job execution.
successful_path: Before functional verification, ensure the mounted Laminar home is writable by the runtime user or have the container entrypoint repair ownership/perms; then restart Laminar and re-run the job verification.
fix: Verify write access for the in-container `laminar` user on the mounted Laminar home before accepting the deployment.
If host ownership cannot be changed, use an entrypoint fallback that relaxes permissions enough for runtime state creation.
precheck: Inspect `ls -ld` for `/var/lib/laminar` and job directories from inside the container.
Require one real `laminarc run` before declaring success; do not stop at the dashboard or `show-jobs`.
anti_pattern: Accepting a Laminar deployment because `/` is 200 and jobs are listed without verifying an actual run.
quick_checks: `find /var/lib/laminar -maxdepth 2 -type f` should include `laminar.sqlite` after a successful run.
`laminarc run hello` should return `<job>:<run>` rather than `Peer disconnected`.
`/archive/hello/<run>/result.txt` should return the expected artifact body.

summary: Manual Buildkite Agent bootstrap verification outside Buildkite can fail for two non-runtime reasons: an empty pull request value can generate refs/pull//head, and a bind-mounted local repo can trip Git safe.directory checks inside the container.
symptom: Manual bootstrap retries fail with fatal invalid refspec refs/pull//head or fatal dubious ownership errors against a mounted repository.
root_cause: The bootstrap checkout path assumes normal Buildkite environment values such as a non-empty pull request marker and a repo clone path that Git inside the container considers safe.
successful_path: For an offline sanity check, prefer buildkite-agent bootstrap with --skip-checkout --phases command. If checkout testing is necessary, set pullrequest to false explicitly and avoid bind-mounted repos unless safe.directory is configured inside the container.
fix: Use --skip-checkout --phases command for minimal offline bootstrap verification.
Set --pullrequest false when invoking bootstrap manually for a non-PR checkout path.
Do not rely on a bind-mounted local git repository inside the container unless Git safe.directory is configured.
precheck: When invoking bootstrap manually, decide whether you need checkout or only command-phase verification.
If using a mounted local repo inside the container, expect Git safe.directory protections.
anti_pattern: Do not interpret refs/pull//head as proof that the agent image is broken.
Do not spend retries on bind-mounted repo checkout when command-phase verification is sufficient.
quick_checks: If bootstrap is only a runtime sanity test, use --skip-checkout --phases command.
If checkout is required, pass --pullrequest false explicitly for non-PR runs.
If cloning from a mounted repo fails with dubious ownership, switch to a network clone or configure safe.directory.

summary: Fluent Bit 5.0.3 rejects the `format` property on the `http` input in YAML config and exits before startup; remove it instead of retrying the container unchanged.
symptom: The container loops in restart state and logs `unknown configuration property 'format'` for the `http` input.
root_cause: The Fluent Bit 5.x `http` input schema allows only `add_remote_addr`, `remote_addr_key`, `success_header`, `tag_key`, and `successful_response_code`, so older or assumed keys like `format` hard-fail initialization.
successful_path: Inspect `docker compose logs`, remove the unsupported `format` key from the `http` input, recreate the container, and then continue verification against the monitoring API and ingest endpoint.
fix: Remove `format` from the `http` input block before retrying startup.
Use the container error output itself as the authoritative schema hint for the plugin.

summary: A GitBucket WAR container that drops privileges can fail on first boot if the mounted home volume stays root-owned or if su strips the Java path; normalize ownership first and execute the Java binary by absolute path after switching users.

Use the absolute Java binary path and export PATH explicitly after su.

Inspect the runtime image's Java path before assuming su will preserve it.

Do not keep retrying compose restarts after the same permission or PATH error appears in logs.

signature: nodebb docker automated setup creates /opt/config/config.json but runtime opens web installer unless CONFIG is exported
summary: NodeBB loader.js reads CONFIG from the environment; pass/export CONFIG=/opt/config/config.json for runtime, not only setup --config.
stack_patterns: Node.js Docker app with generated config volume
symptom: After noninteractive NodeBB setup writes /opt/config/config.json, the public endpoint still serves the web installer page.
root_cause: NodeBB loader.js resolves the runtime config from process.env.CONFIG or config.json; trailing npm/nodebb --config arguments were not sufficient for loader startup in the wrapper.
successful_path: Export CONFIG=/opt/config/config.json in the container entrypoint before running setup and before npm start, then verify homepage, UI asset, and /api/config.

signature: centreon unattended installer named volume etc-centreon permission denied configFileSetup 500 api login 500

signature: kind cluster created from docker-socket toolbox emits kubeconfig server 127.0.0.1:<host-port> unreachable from non-host-network toolbox
summary: Docker-socket kind toolbox containers need host networking, or a host-gateway kubeconfig rewrite, to reach kind API endpoints bound on host localhost.
stack_patterns: toolbox container runs helm and kubectl
symptom: Helm and kubectl report Kubernetes cluster unreachable for https://127.0.0.1:<port> from inside the toolbox container after kind cluster creation succeeds.
root_cause: kind writes a kubeconfig API server endpoint bound to the Docker host loopback, but a default-bridge toolbox container resolves 127.0.0.1 to itself.
successful_path: Set network_mode: host on the toolbox service before running helm/kubectl against the generated kind kubeconfig.
fix: Use Docker Compose network_mode: host for toolbox services that create kind clusters through the host Docker socket.
Alternatively rewrite kubeconfig server to a reachable host-gateway address and add the appropriate extra_hosts entry.
precheck: After kind create cluster, run kubectl version from the same toolbox execution context before Helm install.
Check whether kubeconfig server is https://127.0.0.1:<port>.
anti_pattern: Running helm/kubectl from a default Docker bridge toolbox with an unmodified kind kubeconfig that points to 127.0.0.1.
quick_checks: docker compose run --rm toolbox sh -lc 'kind get kubeconfig --name <cluster> > /bundle/.kubeconfig && KUBECONFIG=/bundle/.kubeconfig kubectl version'
evidence: DP_LOGS/emissary-ingress-v4.1.0-final/deploy.log shows initial localhost connection refusal, then successful Helm install after network_mode: host.
